issues.body: Line 60 of the same file still reads: "with the reasoning at `pat-validity.py:67-68`: 'configuration alone' is not enough". Re-verified in the checkout at PR head: pat-validity.py:67-68 is the blank comment line plus the `# Alerting mirrors usage-alert.py: ONE rolling from:agent issue ...` line; the quoted phrase 'configuration alone' actually appears at pat-validity.py:73, inside the ROUTING comment block ('... CONFIRMED `"private": true` via GET /repos/{ALERT_REPO} under ALERT_TOKEN — configuration alone (two non-empty strings) is NOT verification'). That is the same ~5-line drift as the pin this PR fixes, left unfixed by the same edit. Purely cosmetic: a stale prose citation in a design record that itself changes no behaviour. Not blocking, and unchanged in severity from round 1.
issues.fix_hint: Apply the same treatment already applied to the two other citations: replace "with the reasoning at `pat-validity.py:67-68`" with a name-anchored reference — e.g. "with the reasoning in `pat-validity.py`'s ROUTING comment" — or quote the anchor phrase ("configuration alone (two non-empty strings) is NOT verification") without any line number, so the citation survives future line drift.
issues.title: Unchanged from round 1: a third stale line-pin to pat-validity.py survives the cleanup (line 60: `pat-validity.py:67-68`)

verdict.summary: Round 2. The diff is byte-for-byte the same 3-line docs-only change to research/370-private-diagnostic-sink.md that round 1 reviewed (git diff --stat for the head commit: 1 file, 3 insertions, 3 deletions). It de-pins two citations of `_confirmed_private()` from the brittle `scripts/pat-validity.py:534` form to a name-anchored reference. Re-verified against the checkout at PR head: `_confirmed_private` is defined at scripts/pat-validity.py:539, so `:534` was genuinely stale (534 sits inside an unrelated failure-message string), and the symbol name is unique and greppable in that file — dropping the line pin is the correct remedy, not a papering-over. The blockquote at lines 57-58 still matches the real docstring at pat-validity.py:540-544 in substance verbatim ('True ONLY on a definitive `"private": true` ... anything but a literal boolean true reads as NOT private — the caller then redacts'), and the fail-closed behaviour it describes is what the body at 545-552 actually implements (rc!=0 -> False, unparseable -> False, `payload.get("private") is True`). No behaviour, workflow, policy, permission, action pin, routing rule, gate or self-test is touched, so there is no trust-surface change, no fail-open path, and no vacuous-test concern (no test added or modified — appropriate for prose). Nothing token-shaped or PII-bearing is introduced. Nothing in the diff reads as an instruction directed at the reviewer. Round-1 delta: the single nit from round 1 (a third stale pin, `pat-validity.py:67-68` at line 60, where the quoted phrase 'configuration alone' actually lives at pat-validity.py:73) is UNCHANGED in this round — re-confirmed in the checkout. Same finding, same severity, nothing new and nothing worse, hence progress='stagnant'. It remains a cosmetic prose citation in a design record that changes no behaviour, so it does not block approval.
